outcome: Remove the Django embed: the shell always draws our own frame, and the proxy forwards only the API and file downloads
acceptance_criteria: `frontend/src/shell/FactoryDesk.tsx` no longer exists, and nothing in `frontend/src`, `frontend/tests`, `frontend/e2e` or `frontend/mock` mentions `FactoryDesk`, `work_desk_url`, `django_url`, `factory-forms`, `factory-assets` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_FACTORY_ORIGIN`. — verify: a vitest test using `matchingSources` from `frontend/tests/source-files.ts` over those four folders (excluding the test file itself) returns an empty list; `cd frontend && npm test` passes.

The rewrite set is exactly the expected one. — verify: new `frontend/tests/next-config.test.ts` sets `API_ORIGIN`, calls `rewrites()` and asserts: `beforeFiles` is exactly the `/api/v1/:path*` rewrite; `afterFiles` has exactly six entries whose sources match the table; `fallback` is empty or absent; no source is `/:path*`, `/accounts/...`, `/static/...`, `/factory-forms/...`; every destination starts with `API_ORIGIN`; the config has no `env` key.

`/__mock/reset` is present only with `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOCK_DEMO=1` and non-production. — verify: the same test runs the config with the flag unset (absent), `'1'` (present once), and `'1'` with `NODE_ENV=production` (absent).

Each of the six patterns accepts its route and rejects near misses. — verify: the test converts each source with Next's path matcher (`next/dist/compiled/path-to-regexp`, or `next/dist/shared/lib/router/utils/path-match`) and asserts: a matching example for each (UUID `3f2b8c1e-1a4d-4c7e-9b0a-5d6e7f8a9b0c`, ids `12`) matches; a non-numeric id, a non-UUID case, an extra trailing segment (`/cases/<uuid>/files/1/extra`), and the unrelated `/finance/followup-inbox/<uuid>/key` and `/health` do not match.

No rewrite shadows an app route. — verify: the same test asserts every rewrite sits in `afterFiles`, and that none of the app routes `/work/12`, `/work/12/history`, `/work/12/decide`, `/work/12/outcome`, `/work/12/respond`, `/projects`, `/projects/<uuid>`, `/projects/<uuid>/documents/5`, `/projects/<uuid>/anything` matches any of the six sources.

The shell always draws our frame, even if `/me` still carries Django fields. — verify: a vitest render of `AppShell` (pattern of `frontend/tests/frame-fixtures.test.tsx`) with a `/me` mock body that includes `work_desk_url` and `django_url` destinations draws the standard frame states (ready nav from `destinations`, or the no-sections state), with no `psl-work-client` element and no link whose href contains `/factory-forms` or a `django_url`.

Signed-out, forbidden, error and loading states still draw as before. — verify: the existing shell tests (`frame-fixtures.test.tsx` and the other shell tests) pass unchanged; none is edited to relax an assertion.

Mock dev run unchanged. — verify: `cd frontend && npm run dev -- -p 3101` (mock on `127.0.0.1:4010`, or `MOCK_PORT` set to a free port if 4010 is taken) starts both; the home page and `/my-work` in a browser draw our frame (top nav, bell, page content), the browser console shows no failed request for `/factory-assets/work-client.js`, and Reset demo (DemoBar) still works. `npm run build` succeeds.

Unknown page is a Next 404, not Django JSON. — verify: with the dev run, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3101/no-such-page` prints `404` and the body is the app's `not-found` page (HTML from `frontend/src/app/not-found.tsx`), not `{"error"...page_retired...}`; `/accounts/login/` and `/static/x.js` likewise return the Next 404 and never reach the API origin.

Live API-only check: a signed-out visit shows our frame. — verify (integration owner): start Django with `PSL_DJANGO_UI=0 PSL_ENV=development PGDATABASE=psl PGUSER=psl PGHOST=127.0.0.1 PGPORT=55432` and `python manage.py runserver 127.0.0.1:8000` (Postgres already on 55432, migrated), then `API_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:8000 npm run dev -- -p 3102` (so `dev.mjs` runs the mock only for its own `4010`, with the demo bar off since the origin differs). Open `http://127.0.0.1:3102/` with no session: the page shows `SignedOutState` ("You're signed out." with the Sign in link), plus the frame chrome as drawn; it does not show the Django login widget or a raw JSON 404. `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:3102/api/v1/me` returns the API's 401 JSON through the proxy. Record the commands and the visible result in the build notes. A different state caused only by the v7-shaped `/me` against live data belongs to F-57; note it, do not fix it.

Download routes reach Django and keep its permission checks. — verify: in the live check, `curl -i http://127.0.0.1:3102/cases/3f2b8c1e-1a4d-4c7e-9b0a-5d6e7f8a9b0c/files/1/` (no session) returns Django's own 401/403/404 for that route (from `apps/agents/upload_views.download`, in API JSON form), not the Next 404 HTML, and not file content. Repeat for `/work/1/invoice-proof/1/`. Negative: `/cases/not-a-uuid/files/1/` returns the Next 404 and does not reach port 8000 (confirm in the runserver log).

Lint, typecheck and the gate pass. — verify: `cd frontend && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test`, and `python delivery/design.py check` (or the repo's design check named in `delivery/checks.sh`) reports no new finding.

risk.rationale: Medium. Small diff, but `next.config.ts` decides which paths reach Django, and four of the six routes carry client files and payment proofs; a rewrite that is too broad or that shadows an app route would be a security and routing fault that is easy to miss. Surfaces: ui (shell loses the embed), infra (proxy config, env var removal), security (authenticated download paths exposed through the proxy). No data, money logic, auth code or contract change, so not high; no new flow or copy, so product acceptance is not required.

findings.summary: Criterion 11 expected Django's own 401/403/404 for an unauthenticated download. Django answers 302 to `/accounts/login/` because of `@login_required` (`apps/agents/upload_views.py:57,118`). The browser then lands on a Next 404 until SCR-17. This is existing backend behaviour, outside this feature's lane, and the builder recorded it. It needs a backend or F-57 follow-up so downloads answer an API-form 401. Do not change it here.

`next-config.test.ts` accepts `afterFiles` entries whose destination includes the `:param` names, but it never asserts the exact destination of each download, for example `${API}/work/:work/invoice-proof/:proof/`. The trailing-slash and no-parenthesis checks are enough to catch regressions, so this is only a hardening idea.

A download without a session is a 302 to `/accounts/login/?next=...`, which is a Django 404 `page_retired` in API-only mode (`PSL_DJANGO_UI=0`) and a Next 404 through the proxy. Spec criterion 11 expected an API-form 401/403/404. This is the same as TECH-1-1 and is accepted under D-172. The follow-up is for the backend to answer the download routes with an API-form 401.

A trailing-slash request such as `/cases/<uuid>/files/1/` or `/cases/not-a-uuid/files/1/` gets a Next 308 to the slash-less path before any rewrite. The redirected request is the one proxied, and it reaches Django with the slash added. This works. The only effect is that `curl` without `-L` shows 308, not Django's answer, for the spec's slash example (criterion 11).

Scope the technical and QA reviews left unproved (see Verified-scope table below) must be carried to the named owners and not read as proved. Evidence: review-qa.md "Not proved", build.md criterion 8.

The branch also carries a commit outside the spec's lanes: the `frontend/tests/assistant-dictation.test.ts` repair (path fix plus a holder object in place of the `this` alias). The coordinator requested it, it is a test-only change, and the technical review found no assertion relaxed. It was needed for the gate to pass. Record it in the merge note as a separate item. Other changed paths (architecture v8 package, decisions files, F-57 record, design/review.json) are the planning commits for D-172 and D-173, not feature code.
